description: Portuguese vocabulary register audit list. 'formal' = literary/EP-written item dead in Brazilian conversation; 'preferred' = what Brazilian speakers actually say. Deck targets Brazilian Portuguese: você/vocês default, o senhor/a senhora polite. Severity: 'high' = dead in BR speech, swap wherever it appears in conversational cards; 'medium' = written-leaning, swap in beginner content. See docs/portuguese-register-policy.md.

dead_in_speech.rationale: Literary and European-written morphology that Brazilian speech has abandoned.

entries.note: Dead in all spoken Portuguese; survives in liturgy and archaic texts only.

entries.preferred: vou dizer (para ele) / vai ser feito
entries.note: Written-formal fossil; in Brazil it reads as parody of officialese.
Literary tense. Speech always uses tinha + participle. Fixed expressions (quem me dera) are exempt.
«o homem cujo carro...» → «o homem que o carro dele...» or restructure. Alive in writing, dead in BR conversation.
Essay/report connector; speech says mas or só que.
Bureaucratic purpose connector. The slang «a fim de» (= in the mood for: «tô a fim de pizza») is fully alive and unrelated — exempt.
